title: Why viruses? AAV as a delivery truck
objective: Explain what AAV delivers, and why injecting a virus complements bred-in mouse genetics.

steps.title: Genetics defines the cell; the virus delivers the cargo
steps.body: Bred-in alleles are powerful but fixed — the payload is everywhere the driver fires, from birth. Often you want to deliver a tool **to a specific place, at a specific time, in an adult**. That's what a virus does: you inject it where you want expression.

steps.title: AAV: the workhorse vector
steps.body: **Adeno-associated virus ([[AAV]])** is the standard delivery vehicle in neuroscience. It's small, doesn't cause disease, and gives long-lasting expression without integrating much into the genome. You load it with your payload ([[reporter]], GCaMP, a [[DREADD]]) and inject it. Its cargo capacity is limited (~4.7 kb), which shapes what fits.

steps.prompt: What's the main advantage of delivering a tool by AAV injection rather than breeding it in?
options: It removes any need to run experimental control groups
Spatial and temporal control: you pick where and when it expresses
It permanently rewrites the genome of every cell in the body
It completely does away with the need for any Cre line
steps.explanation: Injection gives you control of location (where you put the needle) and timing (when you inject). It often works WITH a [[Cre]] line, not instead of one (lesson C4-L4).

steps.setup: You want to express a DREADD only in neurons innervating the pancreas, in adult mice.
options: A bred-in allele expressed from birth everywhere the marker is on
Inject an AAV with the DREADD so expression is local and adult-timed
No delivery method is needed; the DREADD appears on its own
Give a drug alone and skip expressing any DREADD at all
steps.reveal: Viral injection lets you target the pancreas pathway in adults. Combined with a Cre line and a Cre-dependent AAV (C4-L4), you get both cell-type AND spatial/temporal specificity — exactly your project's setup.

sources.citation: Wolfson RL, et al. DRG afferents... distal colon. Cell 186:3368-3385 (2023).
sources.note: Uses AAV injection (including retrograde) to access colon-projecting DRG neurons.

reviewNotes: Sets up serotype, retrograde, and Cre-dependent viral payloads.
